$comment: CDISC CORE findings on the Study Data Pipeline that are explained (#2603). Read by scripts/study-data-core.ts reconcile: a CORE finding with no entry fails the workflow, and so does an entry no finding matches. category is defect (tracked by issue), by-design, ct-cache (the declared CT release is not in CORE's cache) or core-limitation (an engine false positive or execution error). Entries with target crf-usdm explain CORE's USDM 4.0 findings on CRF Studio's preset exports (#3051), matched per preset: an entry covers the presets it names, or every preset when it names none, and is stale for any preset it covers that no longer reports it.

entries.reason: AEs with a month-only start date have no EPOCH: an epoch cannot be assigned from a partial date.

Medications started before informed consent have no EPOCH, since they began before the study's first epoch; most are remembered to the month only. Medications for an AE with a month-only start date have none either.
TSVCDVER is the declared CT release, which CORE's rule cache does not hold yet.

The rule compares --DECOD with FAOBJ on any record that RELREC relates, as though the relationship were to a Findings About record. The study has no FA domain: RELREC relates adverse events to the medications given for them, so FAOBJ is absent and every related AE and CM record is reported.

SDTMIG 3.4 MH has no MHSOC variable; MHBODSYS carries the primary system organ class from the study's dictionary, so the rule compares it with a variable the domain does not define.
SDTMIG 3.4 MH has no MHSTDY. History starts years before first dose and is mostly year or year-month only, so MHDY on the collection date is the study day the domain carries.
SDTMIG 3.4 MH has no MHENDY. Resolved conditions ended before screening and are dated to the year or month, so no study day can be derived from them.
